transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. As you know, we have a manufacturing borrower with a $9,000,000 term loan that has missed its most recent scheduled principal payment. The borrower is requesting a 12-month maturity extension and a reduction in its cash interest rate. Before I can make a final underwriting decision on this restructuring, our approval checklist requires each of you — credit risk, banking counsel, relationship management, and loan operations — to state your relevant findings on the record. I also want to flag two specific items that the approval memo must address separately: any borrower cash injection amount and any principal paydown amount. These are independent terms, so please address each distinctly if they apply to your area. Let's go around the table. Could each function please share its finding so I can cite them in the final justification?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: From a loan operations standpoint, I confirmed this morning that our servicing platform can enforce a weekly borrowing-base certificate, and the risk team requires that certificate to be submitted weekly for this restructuring. However, the operating instruction for the weekly borrowing-base certificate is still absent from the draft closing checklist — this needs to be added before we close. On the two items Elena flagged: loan operations has not been informed of any borrower cash injection amount or principal paydown amount, so I cannot speak to either of those terms from my area.

transcript.text: From a banking counsel perspective, I need to flag a critical legal finding that I discovered this week but have not yet circulated. An existing equipment lender's intercreditor agreement requires three distinct closing-package items before we can proceed: first, the equipment lender's written consent before any maturity extension can be granted; second, an amended-loan prohibition on additional liens on the borrower's production equipment must be included; and third, a separate intercreditor-consent commitment must be recorded in the closing package. All three of these items must be satisfied for the 12-month maturity extension the borrower is requesting. On the two items Elena flagged separately — borrower cash injection amount and principal paydown amount — banking counsel has not been informed of any specific amounts for either term, so I cannot speak to those from my area.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: From a credit risk standpoint, I need to share my revised downside analysis, which I completed this morning after receiving the borrower's updated order book. The analysis supports approval only with a 6-month extension — not the 12 months the borrower requested — an exactly $1,000,000 principal paydown, and an 850-basis-point cash interest rate. I should note that this analysis has not yet been attached to the underwriting file. On the two items Elena flagged separately: my analysis specifies a $1,000,000 principal paydown amount as a condition of support. It does not specify a borrower cash injection amount, so I cannot speak to that term from my area.
